literal: In muddy ground where its legs sink, a jackal will kill a male elephant that has faced fearless spear-wielding warriors.
translation: Even a jackal can kill a mighty male elephant, which has faced fearless spear-wielding warriors on the battlefield, if it gets trapped in deep muddy ground where its legs sink.
modern: அஞ்சாத வேல் ஏந்திய வீரர்களைத் தன் முகத்தால் எதிர்த்து நின்ற ஆண் யானையை, அதன் கால் ஆழப் புதையும் சேற்று நிலத்தில் மாட்டித் தவிக்கும்போது, ஒரு நரியும் கொன்றுவிடும்.
explanation: This couplet illustrates the supreme importance of choosing the right place for action. A mighty male elephant is incredibly powerful and can easily face brave warriors armed with spears on a dry battlefield. However, if that same elephant enters a swamp or muddy ground where its heavy legs sink, its immense strength becomes useless. In such a helpless position, even a weak animal like a jackal can easily overpower and kill it. Thus, the couplet teaches that even the most powerful person will be defeated if they fight in an unfavorable location.
